description: Phase 25 and #2042 carried a released exempt ALLOWANCE (an EARN- line) into final pay's annualization. Year end also treats a non-taxable company premium (a PREM- line whose notes say 'Taxable: no') and an exempt leave conversion (a LEAVE_CONV- line whose notes say 'Tax treatment: exempt') as exempt, because the cutoff withheld as if they were not paid. A worker separated at year end must therefore receive the same tax settlement from final pay as year end gives. Phase 32 certifies this through the real engine with three workers hired at the switch on the same salary: a control, a worker with a non-taxable 25.00 an hour company premium (200.00 a cutoff) and a worker with an exempt 10,000.00 leave conversion in cutoff 13. For each, the real computeFinalPay is fed the year-to-date inputs exactly as the Separation API derives them from the released rows, and its tax settlement must equal both the control's and the worker's own year-end settlement.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (up to 10,417 exempt; 10,417 to 16,667: 15%; 16,667 to 33,333: 937.50 + 20%; over 33,333: 4,270.70 + 25% of the excess); annual table (up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000 to 400,000: 15% of the excess over 250,000). Only mandatory SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions and genuinely exempt pay are excluded from taxable compensation (NIRC Sec. 32(B)). A premium the employer's policy classifies as non-taxable, and monetised leave marked exempt, are not compensation subject to the annual tax.
sources.thirteenthMonth: Presidential Decree 851: 13th month pay = one twelfth of basic salary earned in the year; exempt up to 90,000 together with other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)). Neither a company premium nor monetised leave is basic salary.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing, monthly salary 60,000 (30,000 a cutoff), every worker hired 2026-07-01 so only the 12 engine cutoffs 13-24 exist and there are no imported rows. An ordinary cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 100 (1,725); taxable 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 0.20 x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10. Every worker has one complete 8-hour worked Monday in every cutoff so the premium applies; the premium and the conversion do not move any contribution (60,000 is at the SSS and Pag-IBIG ceilings, PhilHealth is on basic) and, being exempt, do not move withholding (Phases 27 and 28).

The premium worker's non-taxable worked-time rule pays 25.00 an hour = 200.00 a cutoff, 2,400.00 over the 12 cutoffs. The conversion worker has 5 days of Vacation Leave at 2,000.00 = 10,000.00 marked tax exempt in cutoff 13.

The Separation API inputs, derived from the released rows exactly as the route does: releasedBasicYtd = sum of BASIC lines = 360,000; thirteenthPaidYtd = 0; grossCompensationYtd = sum over rows of (gross pay - 13th month paid) = 360,000 (control), 362,400 (premium worker) and 370,000 (conversion worker); statutoryContributionsYtd = 20,700; taxWithheldYtd = 12 x 3,259.10 = 39,109.20; releasedExemptAllowanceYtd = the exempt earnings carried into annualization = 0, 2,400 and 10,000.

computeFinalPay: gross for annualization = grossCompensationYtd + 13th month due (30,000); non-taxable = 30,000 pool + contributions 20,700 plus the released exempt earnings; taxable = gross - non-taxable; tax = 15% x (taxable - 250,000); tax adjustment = withheld - tax due (positive = refund). Every worker: taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; refund 25,714.20; net final pay = the 30,000.00 unpaid 13th month + 25,714.20 = 55,714.20.
Year end for each worker equals the control's tax figures: the premium and the conversion are added to gross compensation and to the non-taxable bucket by the same amount.

noExemptEarningControl.description: No policy and no conversion. Year end: gross 390,000; non-taxable 50,700; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; refund 25,714.20. Final pay: tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20, net 55,714.20.

nonTaxableCompanyPremium.description: A non-taxable 25.00 an hour company premium: 200.00 a cutoff, 2,400.00 in all, on 12 PREM- lines marked 'Taxable: no'. Year end: gross 392,400; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 + 2,400 = 53,100; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; refund 25,714.20 (Phase 28). Final pay must agree: grossCompensationYtd 362,400 and released exempt earnings 2,400 give taxable 392,400 - 53,100 = 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20, net 55,714.20. If final pay does not carry the premium as exempt it taxes 2,400.00 more, tax is 13,755.00, the refund 25,354.20 and the employee is under-paid 360.00.

exemptLeaveConversion.description: An exempt 10,000.00 leave conversion (5 days at 2,000.00) in cutoff 13, on one LEAVE_CONV- line marked 'Tax treatment: exempt'. The cutoff withholds as if it were not paid (3,259.10). Year end: gross 400,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 + 10,000 = 60,700; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; refund 25,714.20 (Phase 27). Final pay must agree: grossCompensationYtd 370,000 and released exempt earnings 10,000 give taxable 400,000 - 60,700 = 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20, net 55,714.20. If final pay does not carry the conversion as exempt it taxes 10,000.00 more, tax is 14,895.00, the refund 24,214.20 and the employee is under-paid 1,500.00.

limitations: Only a non-taxable worked-time premium (PREM-) and one exempt leave conversion (LEAVE_CONV-) are exercised. Holiday and rest-day (DAYPREM-), overtime (OTPREM-) and night differential (NDPREM-) premium lines are recognised by year end by the same prefix rule and are not exercised separately.
A year-end termination with no imported periods, other outstanding pay, loans, separation pay, final leave monetisation or prior-employer income, as in Phase 25.
The Separation API route cannot be called from a harness (it needs a session); a source test pins the route expressions the harness reproduces.
Year-end rows already computed under an older rule are replaced only when year end is recomputed.
